findings.location: .claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh:4889-4891 (the review_artifact_unrecorded refusal message) and :4856-4858 (the glob whose order it prints)
findings.evidence: THE CONSTRAINT WAS ALREADY ON THIS TASK. k6re comment dated 2026-09-01T00:31:58Z, titled 'BACKFILL CONSTRAINT discovered by the K3 selector work (2026-09-01) -- this changes requirement (3)': 'qa-gate.sh review-record stamps WRITE time, not review time. Backfilling r2..r8 today would give old iterations new timestamps, so iteration-max and timestamp-max would disagree and the gate would REFUSE... The backfill must either carry real historical at-timestamps, or land under the separate non-governing REVIEW-ARTIFACT-RECONCILED v1 grammar that the corpus scan accepts but the governing selector never matches. The latter was already the plan; this makes it MANDATORY rather than merely preferable.' Same comment: 'The r9/r10 hand-backfill happened to be safe because it was recorded in ascending iteration order... That was luck, not design.' REPRODUCED INDEPENDENTLY, controlled, on i8cx's exact measured shape (12 on disk, r1/r9/r10 recorded, 9 unrecorded -- live figures today at HEAD adaf64d). H1: the shipped refusal prints the 9 files in glob (lexicographic) order -- r11, r12, r2, r3, r4, r5, r6, r7, r8. H2: reconciling in exactly that printed order, every review-record returns ok=true, then review-check.sh gate returns ok=false review_artifact_selection_disagreement and approve refuses rc=4; that refusal names --no-review 1x, --accept-unrecorded-review 0x, review-record 0x. H4 CONTROL: the SAME 12 files in ASCENDING iteration order -> gate ok=true winner=12, approve rc=0. H3: re-recording the highest-iteration artifact last repairs it -- named nowhere. G4: two out-of-order records suffice. AND THE FIX REFUSES ITS OWN TASK: k6re carries 10 artifacts on disk (r1-r10) and ZERO REVIEW-ARTIFACT v1 records -- `review-check.sh recorded-hashes claude-workflow-plugin-k6re` returns {count:0,hashes:[]}, and `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM comments WHERE issue_id='claude-workflow-plugin-k6re' AND text LIKE 'REVIEW-ARTIFACT v1 %'` returns 0 -- both measured BEFORE this review artifact was recorded, which adds an 11th on-disk file and takes the record count 0 -> 1, leaving the unrecorded count at 10. Its own lexicographic backfill order is r1,r10,r2..r9, so last-recorded r9 vs highest r10 -- the same wedge. ENUMERATION the 2026-09-01 comment explicitly asked for ('Before the corpus scan lands, enumerate which live tasks would newly refuse'), never produced, produced here by one dolt query over comments plus sha256 of every docs/reviews file: 5 real tasks would newly refuse -- k6re 10/0/10, i8cx 12/3/9, pqnd 9/5/4, xsu1 9/7/2, 6im2 2/1/1 (on-disk/recorded/unrecorded), 26 unrecorded artifacts total; the 10 impact-report-approve_XXXXXX_* files are correctly never matched by the anchored glob (verified B9). AND 'SORT ASCENDING' IS NOT A SUFFICIENT CURE, measured per task: ascending backfill only works when the globally-highest iteration is itself in the unrecorded set. It is for i8cx (unrecorded [2-8,11,12], max 12 = max overall) and k6re (unrecorded [1-10], max 10 = max overall), and it is NOT for the other three -- 6im2 (unrecorded [1], already-recorded [2]), pqnd (unrecorded [1,2,3,4], already-recorded [5-9]), xsu1 (unrecorded [8,9], already-recorded [1-5,7,10]). For those, ascending order still leaves last-written below max(iteration) and still wedges; the only cure is to additionally re-record the globally-highest artifact LAST, i.e. re-record something already recorded -- an action the refusal never mentions and which looks like a no-op or a mistake to whoever is asked to run it.
findings.description: The check is correct. Its advertised cure is not, and the task's own record said so five days before this round shipped. The refusal tells the operator to run `qa-gate.sh review-record <tid> --file <path>` on each named file, and prints the files in the one order that breaks the task: review-record writes the GOVERNING REVIEW-ARTIFACT v1 grammar stamped at write time, so recording historic rounds in lexicographic order inverts cmd_gate's K3 requirement that highest-iteration and latest-timestamp be the same record. The result is review_artifact_selection_disagreement, whose only signposted escape is --no-review -- the total independent-review waiver the implementer deliberately avoided by adding a narrow --accept-unrecorded-review. So following the gate's own printed instructions, in its own printed order, converts a narrow audited acknowledgement into a blanket waiver of the guarantee this phase exists to enforce. It is deterministic, it lands on all 5 affected live tasks, and it lands on this task first: k6re cannot be approved by its own fix without either the bypass or a backfill that wedges it. On the cure: I first thought ordering the glob numerically would be enough, then measured that it is not -- it fixes i8cx and k6re and still wedges 6im2, pqnd and xsu1, because those three have their highest iteration already recorded, so no ordering of the UNRECORDED set can make last-written coincide with max(iteration). The complete ordering-based rule is a two-step nobody documents: backfill the unrecorded set ascending, THEN re-record the globally-highest artifact last. That is fragile enough that I think it is the wrong layer. In preference order: (1) implement the REVIEW-ARTIFACT-RECONCILED v1 non-governing path the 2026-09-01 comment declares mandatory -- the only cure that never perturbs the governing selector, and independently re-derived here by measurement, though see R13-F2 because recorded-hashes cannot currently see that grammar; (2) failing that, relax cmd_gate's K3 selector to 'highest well-formed iteration, recorded at any time', which dissolves the class outright but needs a read of every K3 consumer; (3) at absolute minimum, and only as a stopgap, state the full two-step rule verbatim in BOTH the review_artifact_unrecorded and review_artifact_selection_disagreement messages, including that the last step re-records an artifact that is already recorded. Ship whichever with a paired negative control: reconcile a pqnd-shaped backlog (highest iteration already recorded -- the case ascending order does NOT fix) in the order the SHIPPED refusal prints, assert approve reaches 0, and mutate the fix away to prove the leg fails without it. A control built on i8cx or k6re alone would pass under the insufficient fix and prove nothing.

findings.location: .claude/scripts/review-check.sh:1875 (the awk guard /^REVIEW-ARTIFACT v1 /) and :1869-1871 (art_prefix_len's anchored regex, which re-anchors the same literal)
findings.evidence: recorded-hashes matches only records beginning `REVIEW-ARTIFACT v1 `. Fed a two-comment fixture containing one REVIEW-ARTIFACT-RECONCILED v1 record (artifact_hash=ABC) and one REVIEW-ARTIFACT v1 record (artifact_hash=DEF), it returns {count:1,hashes:["DEF"]} -- ABC absent. `grep -rn REVIEW-ARTIFACT-RECONCILED --include=*.sh --include=*.md .` (excluding .beads/) returns nothing, so the grammar is not yet implemented, and no bd task exists for it or for the corpus scan.
findings.description: The 2026-09-01 BACKFILL CONSTRAINT comment on this task declares that backfills must land under a separate non-governing REVIEW-ARTIFACT-RECONCILED v1 grammar, mandatory rather than preferable. This fix's acceptance predicate cannot see that grammar, so once it lands, reconciled artifacts will still count as unrecorded and this refusal will keep firing forever on exactly the corpus it was built for. Rated medium rather than high because the grammar is unimplemented today, so this is currently a forward-incompatibility rather than a live defect -- but it is the reason R13-F1 has no safe cure available right now, and it becomes high the moment the reconciled grammar ships. Whichever of the two lands second has to change the other; deciding that now is cheaper than discovering it then.

findings.evidence: The F1 doc-only fast path calls approve with exactly --no-review --no-completion --no-design (verify-before-stop.sh:4539-4544) and has no slot for --accept-unrecorded-review. Reproduced with that exact flag set against qa-gate.sh directly (verify-before-stop.sh never invoked, per constraint). E1: a stray unrecorded artifact NOT in changed-files.txt -> rc=4 review_artifact_unrecorded, so the F1 arm blocks instead of releasing. E2: after review-record on that file -> rc=0, so that recovery does clear it. I1/I2/I3, a before/after pair with a control: on a degraded install (review-check.sh removed) the k6re-stripped build returns rc=0 while the shipped build returns rc=4 review_check_unavailable, and a healthy install returns rc=0 on both -- isolating the degraded-install condition. The new fail-closed arm is reachable precisely because it sits OUTSIDE the bypass_review guard (qa-gate.sh:4836) unlike the REVIEW-SEPARATION copy at the same error_key, which is deliberate and correct.
findings.description: Two new error keys can now block the F1 doc-only Stop arm -- review_artifact_unrecorded and review_check_unavailable -- and neither appears in the enumeration that exists, in its own words, 'so the availability cost is stated rather than discovered'. The second lands on the exact degradation class that comment names as its own reproduction (a partially-synced or half-installed tree). The behaviour is defensible and consistent with the qzv.3 precedent, which explicitly accepted turning an always-release path into one that can block, and the tracker survives either way. What is now false is a load-bearing comment a future agent will consult while debugging an F1 block, fail to find its key in, and conclude the block is impossible.

The orchestrator states it commits on approval, so approving as-is lands the change against a documented convention five consecutive prior commits observed. One entry fixes it.

findings.evidence: B1: with a real task T and a planted artifact at `<sanitized-T>-r2-r1.json` (the canonical path a sibling task whose id is literally `<T>-r2` would use), `compgen -G '<T>-r*.json'` matches BOTH T's own r1 and the sibling's file, and approve refuses rc=4 review_artifact_unrecorded on T. Not reachable with bd-generated ids: every observed suffix is [a-z0-9]{3,4} with sub-tasks using '.' (fkm.8, 94d.1), never '-', so no live id is another id plus '-r<n>'.
findings.description: The read-side glob is one character looser than the write-side derivation: review_artifact_path_for yields exactly one path per (task, iteration), but `-r*` on the read side also spans an embedded '-r<n>-r<n>'. A false refusal, fail-closed, naming the offending file and both escapes, and unreachable under bd's own id generator. A numeric-only wildcard would close it; not worth a fix on its own.

findings.evidence: B5: a DIRECTORY named `<sanitized-tid>-r9.json` inside docs/reviews/ is admitted by [ -e ], hashed, and reported as '(unhashable, rc=1 -- cannot corroborate)' -> rc=4. B6: an EMPTY file likewise, since workflow-manifest.sh hash-file refuses empty by design. Both fail closed.
findings.description: [ -e ] admits any filesystem object; [ -f ] would skip a directory as the non-artifact it is. Current behaviour is safe and arguably preferable for an unexpected shape, but the message says 'unhashable' where 'not a regular file' is the true cause -- and the codex-review.sh spec's C10 leg already treats a directory at the derived path as a distinct named condition, so the vocabulary exists.

findings.evidence: 15.9 proves its mutation landed via cmp -s (differs) and bash -n (parses) but does not assert the footprint. Section 14.4c does: `diff "$RCHECK" "$K6RE_R5_REVERT" | grep -c '^<'` must equal 1. Measured today: `grep -cF '| LC_ALL=C sort -u)' .claude/scripts/review-check.sh` = 1 and the 15.9 sed changes exactly 1 line -- correct now, unguarded against a future second occurrence.
findings.description: 15.9 meets the letter of the pairing requirement's part 1 (a leg proving the mutation landed) but not 14.4c's stricter bar (proving it landed ONLY there) -- and 14.4c's bar is the one this very round had to restore after its first draft doubled the footprint. The same one-line assertion closes the same class at the same cost.

findings.evidence: The Stop hook re-runs review-check.sh gate before releasing, which is what makes a finding recorded AFTER approval re-arm the gate. The unrecorded-artifact predicate is not in that predicate: recorded-hashes has exactly one caller (qa-gate.sh:4864). So an artifact written into docs/reviews/ between a successful approve and the Stop rides through unchecked.
findings.description: One gate end has the check and the other does not, unlike the findings predicate which is wired at both. NOT proposing a third reader -- qa.md forbids that (jio.1), and the Stop hook would be the correct single place if anywhere. Recorded so a later pass does not assume symmetry that is not there; the window is narrow and the harm is the class the fix otherwise closes.
